title: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre - choose the hour the gene goes away
mechanism: A CreER fusion sits inactive in the cytoplasm until tamoxifen is given, at which point it enters the nucleus and recombines a floxed allele. The same genetic lesion applied at different embryonic days produces different phenotypes, because developmental requirements are windowed. This converts a binary genotype into a one-dimensional experimental variable.
intervention: A floxed allele of the target gene crossed to an appropriate CreER driver, with tamoxifen dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
predicted_phenotype: Set by the target and the time. Two measured examples: ShhCreER removal progressively earlier removes progressively more digits; Tbx4 ablation before hindlimb-field expression blocks outgrowth, shortly after onset gives proximal hypoplasia with normal outgrowth and normal Fgf10, and later gives NO limb defect at all.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32
evidence.finding: Conditional Cre deletion of Shh at different times separates a transient early patterning phase from an extended growth phase; progressively earlier removal gives progressive digit loss.
'Loss of Tbx4 during later limb outgrowth produces no limb defects, revealing a brief developmental requirement for Tbx4 function.'

reversibility: The DECISION is reversible up to the moment of dosing; the recombination is not. This is control over onset, not an on/off switch.
lethality_risk: This is the mechanism that REMOVES lethality risk, by letting the gene do its early non-limb jobs before being deleted. It is the reason Shh can be studied in the limb at all without cyclopia.
specificity: Temporal; spatial specificity comes from the driver, not from the inducibility.
difficulty: low-medium. Standard, well-characterised, widely available reagents.
what_we_would_run: Encode in the coupling layer that a genotype-to-phenotype claim with no time index is not composable. Naiche's three-outcomes-from-one-lesion is the anchoring example and it is a one-record change. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Tamoxifen itself affects pregnancy and embryonic development; the published designs handle this, but any new stage series needs vehicle controls.

title: Prx1-Cre - confine the lesion to limb-bud mesenchyme
mechanism: A Prx1 (Prrx1) limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme, with recombination first detectable at E9.5 and essentially complete in all limb mesenchymal cells by E10.5, plus a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme. Cre is NEVER detected in limb-bud ectoderm. So a floxed gene can be removed from the limb mesenchyme and left intact in lung, kidney, heart and allantois.
intervention: Cross any floxed allele to Prx1-Cre. For an inducible version, Prx1-CreER.
predicted_phenotype: Target-dependent, but the decisive property is what it AVOIDS: the lung agenesis that kills Fgf10 nulls, the renal agenesis that kills Grem1 nulls, the allantoic failure that kills Tbx4 nulls, and the cardiac defects of Tbx5 nulls are all outside the Prx1 domain.

evidence.cite: Logan M et al. 2002, Genesis 33:77-80, 'Expression of Cre Recombinase in the developing mouse limb bud driven by a Prxl enhancer'
evidence.finding: 'recombinase activity is first observed in the earliest limb bud at 9.5 dpc. By early to mid bud stages at 10.5 dpc recombination is essentially complete in all mesenchymal cells in the limb. Expression of the Cre recombinase was never detected in the limb bud ectoderm.' Also a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme.

reversibility: None - constitutive Cre. The CreER version adds the time axis.
lethality_risk: This is the single most important lethality-reducing reagent in the design space, and the reason a viable limb-reduced mouse is reachable by routes whose germline nulls are not.
specificity: Limb MESENCHYME only. It does not reach the AER, so ectoderm-acting targets (Wnt3, beta-catenin, p63, AER-FGFs) need a different driver. The craniofacial subset is a real caveat.
difficulty: low. One of the most widely used drivers in skeletal biology.
what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. This route is the page's answer to 'how do you get a limbless mouse that is alive', and it is a reagent, not an idea. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: The craniofacial mesenchyme domain means any Prx1-Cre phenotype needs skull assessment before being called limb-specific.

title: Degron knock-in - remove the PROTEIN in hours, not the gene
mechanism: A degron tag (FKBP12-F36V / dTAG) knocked into the endogenous locus leaves the protein normal until a small molecule is given, at which point the ligase machinery degrades it within hours. Unlike Cre, the depletion is post-translational, far faster than protein turnover after gene deletion, and in some systems washable. This is the only route on this page that could in principle switch a limb signal OFF AND BACK ON inside a single embryonic day.
intervention: Knock a dTAG degron into Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh or Grem1 by zygote editing, then dose the dam with the dTAG ligand at a chosen hour.
predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED for limb genes. What IS measured is the method: in a homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in at Nelfb, dTAG depletion was 'non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages' irrespective of administration route, and acute depletion revealed a stage-specific requirement invisible to a constitutive knockout. No limb gene has been degron-tagged in published work that we found.

evidence.cite: Abuhashem A, Lee AS, Joyner AL & Hadjantonakis AK 2022, Dev Cell 57:1068-1080.e6, 'Rapid and efficient degradation of endogenous proteins in vivo identifies stage-specific roles of RNA Pol II pausing in mammalian development'
evidence.finding: A homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in mouse at Nelfb; 'irrespective of the route of administration the dTAG system is non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages'. Acute depletion revealed a specific role in zygote-to-2-cell development.

evidence.cite: Antczak W et al. 2026, Commun Biol 9(1), 'Degron models: a toolbox for rapid in vivo depletion of essential proteins regulating mRNA metabolism'
evidence.finding: Seven degron-tag mouse models by direct zygote editing. 'Degron tags occasionally cause phenotypes that can be mitigated by tag position or tagging system change. In cells, both approaches yield rapid and sustained degradation. In mice, dTAG depletion is effective but varies by protein and administration route, whereas BromoTag shows no in vivo activity.'

reversibility: The highest of any route here IN PRINCIPLE - ligand washout should restore protein. Whether a limb bud recovers after a transient depletion is an empirical question nobody has asked, and it is the most interesting unasked question on this page.
lethality_risk: Low by design: the protein is present for every requirement outside the chosen window.
specificity: Temporal and protein-level; NOT spatial. The ligand reaches the whole embryo, so a degron depletes the target everywhere at once. Pairing it with a tissue-restricted system is not solved.
difficulty: high but decreasing. The honest caveats are in the second paper: tags sometimes cause phenotypes on their own, efficiency varies by protein and route, and one of the two tagging systems showed no in vivo activity at all.
what_we_would_run: Nothing. This is a clearly-labelled proposal and belongs on the page as the frontier method rather than as a result. It is also the most likely answer if a modern reviewer asks 'why would you make a germline mutant at all'. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does transient depletion of a limb signal give a REVERSIBLE limb defect, a permanent one, or none? Unknown, and it is the experiment that would most change how this subject is taught.
Degron depletion is systemic. Combining acute temporal control with limb-restricted delivery is an open engineering problem.

title: RECOMMENDED: limb-restricted, stage-selected Fgf10 removal
mechanism: Take the lesion with the strongest, most unambiguous limb phenotype in the literature - loss of FGF10, which abolishes AER formation and so abolishes the limb - and apply it only where and only when you want it. Prx1-CreER restricts recombination to limb-bud mesenchyme, where FGF10 is actually made, and the tamoxifen dose sets the hour. Everything that kills the germline Fgf10 null (lung, thyroid, pituitary, salivary gland) lies outside the Prx1 domain and outside the induction window.
intervention: Fgf10 conditional (floxed) allele crossed to Prx1-CreER. Tamoxifen at a chosen day. Forelimb-restricted and hindlimb-restricted variants can be approached instead through Tbx5-conditional (forelimb) or Tbx4-conditional (hindlimb) alleles if a single-pair phenotype is wanted.
predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED. We did not find a published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series and will not state its phenotype. The components are each measured: Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives absent limbs; Prx1-Cre recombines all limb mesenchyme by E10.5 and never the ectoderm; CreER timing converts a fixed lesion into a stage series. The honest claim is that this is the best-supported DESIGN, not a known result.

evidence.cite: Min H et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3156-61
evidence.finding: Fgf10 loss abolishes limb bud initiation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; Fgf10 is necessary for AER formation and acts upstream of Fgf8. Perinatal lethality is from absent lungs, a defect in a tissue outside the Prx1 domain.
Prx1 limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5, complete by E10.5, never in limb-bud ectoderm.
Demonstrates for Tbx4 that the same conditional lesion applied at three different times gives three different outcomes, including none - the general principle this design depends on.

reversibility: Onset is chosen; the recombination is permanent. For true reversibility the degron route is the only candidate.
lethality_risk: LOW, and this is the entire point. The germline Fgf10 null is perinatally lethal from lung agenesis; a Prx1-restricted deletion should not touch the lung. We say 'should' because we found no published viability data for this exact cross.
specificity: Limb mesenchyme, both pairs, with a craniofacial caveat from the driver. A single-pair version (Tbx5 for forelimb, Tbx4 for hindlimb) is substantially more likely to give a viable adult.
difficulty: medium. Every component is an existing, published reagent; the work is breeding, dosing and skeletal analysis, not invention.
what_we_would_run: Before any animal: score the predicted severity ordering across induction times with our pattern simulators, pre-register it, and state explicitly that the simulation is not calibrated and the prediction is a hypothesis. We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm; the proposal is a design, and we would present it as one. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Does a Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox animal survive to adulthood? Unknown to us.

Is mesenchymal Fgf10 deletion after E10.5 sufficient to remove a limb, or has the AER already become self-sustaining? The Barrow beta-catenin result shows an existing AER CAN be made to disappear, but that was an ectodermal manipulation, not a mesenchymal one.
